title: Non-blocking findings from backend-ibkr-import-entry-date-from-trades-followups's PR re-review (#410, round 2)
description: pr-reviewer's re-review of PR #410 (backend-ibkr-import-entry-date-from-trades-followups), after the fix for pr-decision's round-2 override (the dateless-SELL-row false-positive-match finding) landed, accepted the PR outright. Two genuinely non-blocking findings surfaced during that re-review's forward-looking check for 'any remaining path of the same shape' and are tracked here so they aren't lost once the PR merges. backend-ibkr-import-entry-date-from-trades-followups-followups.json (the prior <id>-followups task) is already `done` (closed as superseded by the round-2 fix), so this is filed one level deeper per the naming convention CLAUDE.md documents for exactly this case.

checklist.step:
`_parse_account_trades` (`backend/app/data/ibkr_provider.py`) drops a row entirely when `side` can't be recognized (`_parse_trade_side` returns `None`) or when `quantity`/`size` is missing/non-positive -- for a row that was actually a SELL, this removes its quantity from `_derive_entry_date`'s net-of-sells subtraction exactly the same way a dateless dropped SELL row did before this PR's fix, which can manufacture the same kind of false-positive exact quantity match (net pushed upward instead of toward the safe `today()` fallback). Unlike the just-fixed `trade_date` case, there is no equivalent mitigation available here: an unparseable `side` means the row's quantity can't be attributed to either bucket (buy vs. sell) at all, and an unparseable/non-positive `quantity` means there's no magnitude to keep even if the side were known -- so 'keep the row, just don't trust the one field `_derive_entry_date` doesn't read' (the fix applied to dates) doesn't generalize to these two fields. Assessed as lower real-world risk than the `trade_time`/`trade_time_r` case was (`side`/`size` are core fields every real trade row needs to be interpretable as a trade at all -- not a two-field fallback where one documented alternative could plausibly be absent -- and PR #410's own review already noted IBKR's live swagger has no `required` list for ANY field, including these, so this isn't a new weaker guarantee), but nobody has done the explicit directional-risk derivation for `side`/`quantity` that this round's `pr-decision` override did for `trade_date` -- worth recording that derivation explicitly (in the relevant docstrings) and/or deciding whether the residual risk is worth guarding against (e.g., treating an ambiguous-side row conservatively as a SELL for the subtraction, since that's the direction that can never manufacture a false positive) next time someone is in this file.

RESOLVED (2026-10-10, this task): see this task's `decisions` entry for the full directional derivation and the mitigation implemented (defensive side-bucketing for the unparseable-`side`-but-valid-`quantity` case; per-conid poisoning for the no-usable-quantity case).

`_derive_entry_date`'s invariant that every `IBKRTrade` with `side=="BUY"` reaching it has a non-`None` `trade_date` (which makes the `min(t.trade_date for t in buys if t.trade_date is not None)` filter purely a mypy-satisfying no-op, not a runtime guard, per that line's own comment) is enforced only by `_parse_account_trades` being the single production call site that constructs `IBKRTrade` -- confirmed by grep (`grep -rn 'IBKRTrade(' app/` finds exactly one construction site). Nothing enforces this at the type level (`IBKRTrade.trade_date: date | None` permits `None` regardless of `side`) or via a runtime guard on `IBKRTrade` itself (a frozen dataclass with no `__post_init__` check) -- a hypothetical future second construction site for `IBKRTrade` that didn't replicate `_parse_account_trades`'s exact BUY-vs-SELL drop discipline could silently reintroduce a 'skip this buy, derive from a later one instead' wrong-but-plausible-`entry_date` risk, structurally the same shape of bug this task line has now been bitten by twice. Empirically confirmed this round that `coverage.py` does not instrument branch coverage inside a generator expression's own `if` filter clause (a minimal repro: a genexpr `min(x for x in xs if x is not None)` exercised only with the `True` branch still reports 0/0 branches, 100% coverage) -- so a regression here would not even show up as a coverage drop on this line, the usual safety net this project leans on. Low current risk (one call site, correctly guarded, well documented) but worth either a `__post_init__` assertion on `IBKRTrade` (a BUY row's `trade_date` must not be `None`) or a comment at any future second construction site pointing back at this invariant, if this module grows another way to build an `IBKRTrade`.

RESOLVED (2026-10-10, this task): added `IBKRTrade.__post_init__`, raising `ValueError` if `side=="BUY"` and `trade_date is None`. See this task's `decisions` entry.

decisions.decision: For checklist item 1 (unparseable `side`/unusable `quantity`), implemented two distinct, independently-derived mitigations rather than one blanket rule: (a) a row whose `side` can't be recognized but whose `quantity` IS usable is now defensively bucketed as `side="SELL"` instead of dropped; (b) a row whose `quantity`/`size` is missing/unparseable/non-positive is still just dropped when its (confirmed) `side` is `"BUY"` (unchanged, already safe), but now POISONS that row's conid -- recorded in a new `IBKRAccountTrades.poisoned_conids: frozenset[int]` returned alongside `trades` from `_parse_account_trades`/`IBKRProvider.get_account_trades()` -- whenever the row is a confirmed `"SELL"` or its `side` is ALSO unrecognized. `_derive_entry_date` (`app/api/routers/ibkr.py`) gained a `poisoned_conids` parameter and now short-circuits to the `fallback` (today()) branch unconditionally for any conid in that set, skipping the quantity match entirely rather than computing it against only the trades that did parse.
decisions.rationale:
Did the explicit directional derivation the task asked for, for both fields, rather than taking pr-decision's suggested mitigation on faith:

(1) Unparseable `side`, quantity `q` otherwise valid: the row's true side is unknown but its magnitude is known. Dropping it entirely (the prior behavior) contributes 0 to `net` -- safe if the true side was BUY (net ends up below the true value, by `q`, which can only turn a would-be match into a conservative mismatch, never the reverse -- `_derive_entry_date`'s own docstring already establishes true `net` can never exceed `held`), but UNSAFE if the true side was SELL (net ends up `q` ABOVE the true value, which is exactly the false-positive mechanism PR #410 already fixed for dates). Bucketing the row as `"SELL"` instead contributes `-q`: if the true side was SELL, this is the EXACT correct contribution (net equals the true value, zero risk by construction, since a correct net can never exceed `held` either); if the true side was BUY, this contributes `-q` where the truth was `+q` -- net ends up `2q` BELOW the true value, i.e. even further in the already-established-safe direction than dropping was. So bucketing-as-SELL dominates dropping: it's safe in both possible true-side branches, closes the false-positive risk entirely for this sub-case, and only costs an occasional missed derivation (a false negative) when the true side was actually BUY -- which is this feature's own already-accepted tradeoff direction (see PR #410's own `decisions` entry: a lost derivation is tolerated, a wrong one is not). This resolves pr-decision's 'trades one failure direction for another' characterization more precisely than that phrasing suggested: there is no new failure direction introduced, only a reduction in legitimate-derivation frequency traded for eliminating a false-positive path that existed before.

(2) Missing/unparseable/non-positive `quantity`: there is no magnitude left to bucket either way, so no analogous 'keep but reinterpret' fix exists -- confirmed by re-deriving from scratch, not just restating the task's own framing. If the row's side is confirmed BUY, dropping it is still safe (established above: dropping/omitting a BUY's contribution only ever decreases `net` below the true value). If the row's side is confirmed SELL, or unrecognized (so SELL can't be ruled out), dropping it risks the exact same false-positive mechanism as the already-fixed dateless-SELL case, with no cheaper fix available. Considered and rejected three alternatives: (i) poisoning on EVERY dropped row regardless of side -- rejected per the task's own steer, since a confirmed-BUY-with-bad-quantity drop is provably safe and poisoning it would disable derivation more often than the actual risk requires, for zero safety benefit; (ii) inventing a placeholder quantity (e.g. 0 or the held quantity itself) to keep the row 'as a SELL' -- rejected as fabricating data with no basis, strictly worse than admitting the conid is unreconcilable; (iii) representing poisoning via a sentinel `IBKRTrade` row (e.g. `quantity=math.inf`) smuggled into the existing `list[IBKRTrade]` return value instead of a new typed field -- rejected as inconsistent with this task line's own established preference for explicit `Optional` typing over a sentinel value (see `backend-ibkr-import-entry-date-from-trades-followups`'s `decisions` entry, which chose `trade_date: date | None` over a sentinel date for exactly this reason: a sentinel requires every future reader to remember not to misread it, where a real type doesn't), and because `IBKRTrade.quantity` is documented as 'always strictly positive' -- smuggling in a non-representative value would violate that invariant's spirit even if it technically satisfied `> 0`. The chosen fix (a new `IBKRAccountTrades` dataclass with an explicit `poisoned_conids: frozenset[int]`, threaded through `get_account_trades`/`_derive_entry_date`) makes the 'this conid is unreconcilable' fact visible and type-checked rather than implicit.

Tests: added `test_unrecognized_side_with_a_valid_quantity_is_bucketed_as_sell_not_dropped`, `test_non_string_side_with_a_valid_quantity_is_bucketed_as_sell_not_dropped`, `test_unrecognized_side_with_an_unusable_quantity_poisons_the_conid`, `test_confirmed_sell_with_an_unusable_quantity_poisons_the_conid`, and renamed/extended `test_non_positive_quantity_is_dropped` to `test_non_positive_quantity_on_a_confirmed_buy_is_dropped_not_poisoned` (asserting `poisoned_conids == frozenset()`) in `backend/tests/unit/data/test_ibkr_provider.py`; added `test_entry_date_falls_back_for_a_poisoned_conid_even_when_the_remaining_trades_would_have_matched` in `backend/tests/integration/test_ibkr_portfolio_preload.py` (mirrors PR #410's own dateless-SELL counterexample shape: visible trades alone would exactly match `held`, but a poisoned conid must still fall back). Mutation-tested all four behaviors directly (not just re-read the assertions): (1) reverting the `side is None` branch back to `continue` (drop instead of bucket) fails both bucketing tests; (2) removing the `if side != "BUY": poisoned_conids.add(conid)` line fails both poisoning-production unit tests; (3) removing `_derive_entry_date`'s `if position.conid in poisoned_conids: return fallback, False` short-circuit fails the poisoning-consumption integration test (confirming the integration test, which stubs `poisoned_conids` directly rather than deriving it, is actually exercising the router's own consumption of the flag, not just its stub plumbing). Full backend suite (1655 tests, up from 1649) passes at 99.95% coverage (100% on both changed files); ruff/mypy clean; `openapi.json` re-exported byte-identical (no route/schema touched); `scripts/validate_tasks.py` clean.

decisions.decision: For checklist item 2, added `IBKRTrade.__post_init__`, raising `ValueError` if `side == "BUY"` and `trade_date is None` -- a cheap runtime guard on top of (not instead of) the existing single-call-site discipline and the `is not None` mypy-narrowing filter in `_derive_entry_date`'s `min(...)`.
decisions.rationale: The finding's own framing ('cheap to add... if this module grows another way to build an IBKRTrade') matches reality: this is a genuine invariant of the type's own meaning (a BUY row's date is definitionally knowable, per `_parse_account_trades`'s docstring), not an arbitrary restriction, so the guard costs nothing in the one, already-correct production path and fails loudly at construction time in any future path that doesn't replicate the discipline -- closing exactly the gap PR #410's review identified (coverage.py's own empirically-confirmed blind spot for a genexpr's `if` filter clause meant a regression here wouldn't show up as a coverage drop either). Did not restructure `IBKRTrade` into two separate BUY/SELL subtypes (the type-level alternative the finding also floated) -- rejected as disproportionate: it would ripple through every call site that currently pattern-matches on `.side` (`_derive_entry_date`'s `t.side == "BUY"`/`"SELL"` filters, every test's `IBKRTrade(side=...)` construction) for a benefit (static enforcement) the `__post_init__` guard already delivers at runtime, for one single, well-isolated, already-correct call site. Added `TestIBKRTradePostInit` (`backend/tests/unit/data/test_ibkr_provider.py`) with three tests (BUY+real date is fine, BUY+None date raises, SELL+None date is fine); mutation-tested by removing `__post_init__` entirely, which fails `test_buy_with_none_trade_date_raises` as expected -- confirming the guard, not merely the test's own assertion, is what's load-bearing.
